digest.component_or_area: code-review impact-model and gate routing (v3→v4 redesign)
propositions: The code-v3 impact model discards prod_impact and trigger_likelihood fields for maint-lane findings, preventing test-sufficiency findings from blocking even when they guard high-reach paths, because churn dampening compresses maint scores to ~0.30 below advisory threshold.

A single commit shipped a contract declaring stale>0 allowed (exit 0) and a co-located test asserting stale=0, creating an undetected contradiction (bug dystopian-bardlike-basil) that code-v3 review missed because the contract-assertion antipattern was not recognized and prod_impact was discarded.

The code-v4 redesign must introduce forbids_contract_allowed_state as a serious maint binary (undamped ×1.0), re-scope prod_impact/trigger_likelihood to rate guarded-path user reach rather than file type, implement lane-scoped trigger maps and consequence-lane-only reversibility floor, and flip tests to blocking@0.54 to capture 99 high-friction changes (8.0% vs v3's 3.4%) with zero demotions of currently-blocking findings.

Stored code-v3 sidecars must not be rewritten; version gating and offline replay analysis preserve historical audit trail while enabling v4 consumption of previously-discarded prod_impact field for new findings.

Unit, integration, eval, and replay testing must verify v4 lane-split arithmetic (serious undamped; moderate prod-impact-keyed; debt amplifier-only), the new binary's emission with both-halves-verbatim evidence, consequence-lane floor restriction, and median HIGH/NIT separation >0.30 over impact_labels fixture.

Eight consumer sites (two test modules with equality pins, five test premise rewrites, two eval specs) and replay script must be updated to reflect code-v4 version bump and 8-member blocking set including tests@0.54 with ticket citation.
